issues.legal_issue: An executing court may adjudicate a decree-holder’s application under Order XXI Rule 97 when any person obstructs delivery of possession, including a person claiming an independent right in the property.

An application raising objections to execution under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be treated in substance as an application under Order XXI Rule 97 where the objection concerns obstruction to delivery of possession.
An executing court cannot use Section 47 or Order XXI Rule 101 to reconsider matters that could have been raised and decided in the original suit or to go behind the decree.

A person claiming protection as a cultivating tenant cannot invoke the Tamil Nadu Cultivating Tenants’ Protection Act for a period before registration as a tenant, absent an independently established right to possession.

The decree for specific performance and possession was enforceable against the obstructing occupants, whose asserted tenancy and possession did not establish a bona fide independent right to resist execution.
An executing court may permit amendment of an execution petition to give effect to the relief granted by the decree.
Execution proceedings should ordinarily be disposed of within six months, subject to recorded reasons for any extension.
